clinicalPearls: C1q deficiency is the complement defect most strongly associated with early-onset systemic lupus erythematosus, often with prominent cutaneous and central nervous system disease.
It is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner and usually presents in childhood.
Impaired clearance of apoptotic cells and immune complexes is the key mechanism linking the deficiency to lupus-like autoimmunity.
There is also increased susceptibility to encapsulated and pyogenic infections owing to defective classical-pathway activation.
The CH50 (total classical-pathway haemolytic complement) is markedly reduced or absent, while the alternative-pathway assay (AH50) is preserved.
Specific C1q antigenic and functional assays confirm the diagnosis after an absent CH50 is found.
Some patients have functionally defective C1q with normal antigen levels, so functional testing matters.
Management centres on treating the autoimmune disease, vaccination against encapsulated organisms and prompt treatment of infection.
reference.pathophysiology: C1q is the recognition subunit of the first component of the classical complement pathway, binding immune complexes and the surfaces of apoptotic cells. In C1q deficiency the classical pathway cannot be activated, so opsonisation and lysis of certain pathogens are impaired, predisposing to pyogenic infection. Critically, C1q also tethers apoptotic cell debris for clearance by phagocytes; without it, dying cells and nuclear antigens accumulate, are inadequately removed and provoke a break in self-tolerance. This drives the strong association with systemic lupus erythematosus, in which autoantibodies form against these persisting nuclear self-antigens. Defective clearance of circulating immune complexes further contributes to tissue deposition and inflammation.
additionalDifferentials: Idiopathic systemic lupus erythematosus without complement deficiency

additionalInvestigations: CH50 classical-pathway haemolytic assay (markedly low or absent)
C1q antigenic level and functional activity
Genetic testing of the C1q genes
Autoimmune serology including ANA and anti-dsDNA
Renal function and urinalysis for lupus nephritis
Documentation of vaccination status and infection history
redFlags: Invasive infection with encapsulated organisms or signs of meningitis or sepsis
Early-onset severe photosensitive or ulcerating skin disease
reference.prognosis: Outcome is largely determined by the severity of associated lupus and the frequency of serious infections; the majority of individuals with complete deficiency develop lupus-like disease. Vigilant management of autoimmunity and infection prophylaxis improve outcomes.
pitfalls: Overlooking an inherited complement defect in a child presenting with early, severe lupus.
Stopping at an absent CH50 without measuring individual components to localise the defect.
Missing functionally defective C1q when only the antigen level is checked.
Neglecting vaccination and infection prophylaxis against encapsulated organisms.
Attributing persistently low complement solely to disease activity rather than a primary deficiency.

management: Manage the associated systemic lupus erythematosus with standard immunosuppression, using hydroxychloroquine, corticosteroids and agents such as mycophenolate, azathioprine or rituximab according to organ involvement

Prevent infection by vaccinating against encapsulated organisms including pneumococcus, meningococcus and Haemophilus influenzae type b, and treat pyogenic infection promptly, with antibiotic prophylaxis where indicated
Treat and monitor lupus manifestations, particularly the prominent cutaneous, central nervous system and renal (lupus nephritis) disease
Advise photoprotection and skin care for cutaneous lupus
Monitor renal function and urinalysis, autoantibodies, disease activity and, in children, growth
Consider fresh frozen plasma as a source of C1q in selected severe cases, with haematopoietic stem cell transplantation reported for refractory disease
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across paediatric rheumatology, immunology and nephrology
Offer genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive inheritance
